title: Invertible sheaves on a split torus over a normal locally Noetherian scheme
statement: Let $X$ be a locally Noetherian scheme [def-pc-scheme, pqf-def-locnoeth] such that every local ring is an integrally closed domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]. Let $r\geq0$. Put $D=\mathbf Z[z_1^{\pm1},\ldots,z_r^{\pm1}]$, the ring of finite sums $\sum_{u\in\mathbf Z^r}c_u z^u$, with unique coefficients and multiplication $z^uz^v=z^{u+v}$. Let $Y=X\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z}\operatorname{Spec}D$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-pc-fibre-product], let $q:Y\to X$ be projection, and let $e:X\to Y$ be the section induced by $z_i\mapsto1$. Equivalently, over an affine open $\operatorname{Spec}R\subseteq X$ the scheme $Y$ is $\operatorname{Spec}R[z_1^{\pm1},\ldots,z_r^{\pm1}]$ with these coefficient and evaluation maps. For every invertible $\mathcal O_Y$-module $N$ [def-sc-invertible-module] there is an isomorphism of $\mathcal O_Y$-modules $q^*e^*N\cong N$, where pullback is tensor inverse image [def-pc-module-pullback]. Empty and disconnected $X$, and $r=0$, are included; no group action or ampleness is assumed.

source.place: Agent-formulated consequence of Tag 0BD7 (lemma-in-image-pullback) and Tag 0BDA (lemma-open-subscheme-UFD). Apply 0BD7 to the Laurent-space projection on each open normal integral component; its generic fibre is a principal open of affine space over a field, covered by 0BDA. This is not asserted to be the verbatim statement of either tag.

proof.text: First decompose $X$ into disjoint open normal integral schemes $X_a$. Here is the locally Noetherian reduction, without assuming that $X$ is quasi-compact. Choose an affine Noetherian open cover as in [pqf-def-locnoeth]. Each member $U$ is normal because its local rings are those of $X$, so [rem-pc-regular-normal](2) decomposes $U$ into finitely many disjoint open normal integral components. For a global irreducible component $C$ of $X$, [lem-sc-components-open-injection] says that every nonempty $C\cap U$ is a component of $U$. Thus $C\cap U$ is open in $U$, and $C$ is open in $X$. Distinct global components cannot meet: in an affine neighbourhood of a proposed intersection they would give distinct intersecting components, contradicting the injectivity in that same node and the disjointness just obtained. The components cover $X$; each is nonempty and irreducible, and its local rings are the original normal domains, so its open subscheme structure is reduced and integral [def-pc-integral-scheme]. Each $X_a$ remains locally Noetherian by [pqf-def-locnoeth].

source.place: Tag 033N, lemma-normal-locally-Noetherian; deduced explicitly from the Noetherian case of Tag 033M and restriction of components to opens.

proof.text: Over any affine open $\operatorname{Spec}R$ of $X_a$, put $P=R[t_1,\ldots,t_r]$ and $f=t_1\cdots t_r$ (the empty product is $1$). The coefficient presentation in the statement identifies $q^{-1}(\operatorname{Spec}R)$ with $\operatorname{Spec}P_f$. Explicitly, $P_f\to R[z_1^{\pm1},\ldots,z_r^{\pm1}]$ sends $t_i\mapsto z_i$ and $1/f\mapsto\prod_i z_i^{-1}$; its inverse sends $z_i\mapsto t_i$ and $z_i^{-1}\mapsto(\prod_{j\ne i}t_j)/f$. The two maps are inverse on all generators. By clause (0) of [lem-weil-pbc-affine-ideals-closed-subscheme], $\operatorname{Spec}P_f$ is the principal open $D(f)$ of $\operatorname{Spec}P$, with its scheme structure: its coordinate ring is $P_f$ and the inclusion is induced by localization. All identifications commute with restrictions in $R$ because they send each coefficient and each named monomial to itself.

source.place: Tags 0BD7 and 0BDA, Laurent-space application; principal-open localization calculation supplied by the worker.

proof.text: Write $q_a:Y_a=q^{-1}(X_a)\to X_a$. The polynomial projection $\operatorname{Spec}P\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ is flat by [lem-nagata-polynomial-projection-flat]. Its restriction to the open $D(f)$ has the identical source local rings at its points, hence is flat by [def-weil-flat-morphism]. These charts cover $Y_a$, proving flatness of $q_a$. The $R$-algebra $R[z_1^{\pm1},\ldots,z_r^{\pm1}]$ is generated by the $2r$ elements $z_i,z_i^{-1}$, so $q_a$ is locally of finite type by [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Since $X_a$ is locally Noetherian, [pqf-lem-locnoeth-lft] makes $Y_a$ locally Noetherian as well. For $r=0$ the same statements hold for the identity projection.

source.place: Tag 0BD7, lemma-in-image-pullback, hypotheses (1), (3), (4); checked on the Laurent charts.

proof.text: For $x\in X_a$ put $K=\kappa(x)$. The fibre is $\operatorname{Spec}K[z_1^{\pm1},\ldots,z_r^{\pm1}]$: [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] identifies its coordinate ring with $K\otimes_R R[z_i^{\pm1}]$, and the inverse coefficient maps $c\otimes\sum b_u z^u\mapsto\sum cb_u z^u$ and $\sum c_u z^u\mapsto\sum c_u\otimes z^u$ give this ring isomorphism. By step 2 this fibre is $D(t_1\cdots t_r)$ in $\operatorname{Spec}K[t_1,\ldots,t_r]$. The polynomial ring is a domain by [lem-sfb-polynomial-field-ufd], and the displayed monomial is nonzero. Its localization is therefore a nonzero domain (a zero fraction has zero numerator). Its zero ideal is prime, so the spectrum is nonempty and integral by [def-pc-integral-scheme]. Thus every residue-field fibre of $q_a$ is integral and nonempty.

source.place: Tag 0BD7, lemma-in-image-pullback, hypothesis (3); explicit fibre calculation.

proof.text: Let $\eta_a$ be the generic point of $X_a$ and $K=\kappa(\eta_a)$. By step 4 the generic fibre of $q_a$ is an open subscheme of affine $r$-space over $K$. The restriction of $N$ to it is invertible: a local free rank-one frame pulls back to $1\otimes$ that frame by [def-sc-invertible-module, def-pc-module-pullback]. Hence [lem-sfb-affine-space-open-invertible-trivial] makes this restriction trivial. Apply [lem-sfb-normal-noetherian-generic-line-pullback] to $q_a$ and $N|_{Y_a}$. The base $X_a$ is normal integral and locally Noetherian by step 1, the source is locally Noetherian and the map is flat and locally of finite type by step 3, and its fibres are integral nonempty by step 4. Generic-fibre triviality was just proved, so every hypothesis of that node holds. It yields an invertible module $M_a$ on $X_a$ and an isomorphism $\alpha_a:q_a^*M_a\xrightarrow{\sim}N|_{Y_a}$.

source.place: Tag 0BDA, lemma-open-subscheme-UFD, final sentence, followed by Tag 0BD7, lemma-in-image-pullback, hypotheses (1)--(5) and conclusion.

proof.text: The identity section restricts to $e_a:X_a\to Y_a$ and satisfies $q_ae_a=\mathrm{id}_{X_a}$, since evaluating a coefficient at $z_i=1$ returns that coefficient. Pulling $\alpha_a$ back along $e_a$ and using the composition and identity isomorphisms of [def-pc-module-pullback] gives $\beta_a:M_a\xrightarrow{\sim}e_a^*(N|_{Y_a})$. Consequently $\alpha_a\circ q_a^*(\beta_a^{-1})$ is an isomorphism $q_a^*e_a^*(N|_{Y_a})\xrightarrow{\sim}N|_{Y_a}$. This uses existence of $\alpha_a$ only; it requires no uniqueness or canonical choice in the generic-line descent theorem.

source.place: Tag 0BD7, consequence for a morphism with a section; pullback and inverse composition written out by the worker.

proof.text: The open subschemes $Y_a=q^{-1}(X_a)$ are pairwise disjoint and cover $Y$. Restriction of tensor inverse image to these opens is the tensor inverse image for $q_a,e_a$ [def-pc-module-pullback], so step 6 supplies the desired isomorphism on each $Y_a$. They assemble into a global module isomorphism: on an open $V\subseteq Y$, the sheaf axiom for the disjoint cover $V=\coprod_a(V\cap Y_a)$ identifies sections with the product of the component sections; apply the component isomorphisms coordinatewise, and their inverses coordinatewise. These maps commute with restriction and with scalars. This proves $q^*e^*N\cong N$. If $X$ is empty the cover has no members and the same sheaf argument applies. For $r=0$, $q=e=\mathrm{id}$, in agreement with this construction.

source.place: Tags 0BD7 and 0BDA, componentwise application; disjoint-open gluing supplied by the worker.

from.place: Relative torus quotient input: invariant affine covering of the normal ample source after finite étale splitting of the torus. This is the relative-base replacement for the field-only Sumihiro lemma. Supporting input: Equivariant projective embedding before selecting boundary-avoiding weight charts. Supporting first step: linearize a positive tensor power of the initial relatively very ample line before choosing weight sections. Supporting geometric input: invertible sheaves on the product of a locally Noetherian normal scheme with a split torus are pulled back from the identity section; no group action is part of this input.

split_report.summary: No new nodes. Reused generic-line pullback and affine-space-open line triviality; verified Laurent localization, flatness, local finite type, local Noetherianity and integral nonempty fibres. Derived disjoint integral components from the existing Noetherian decomposition and open-component injection, and used the identity section to identify the descended line. The statement is unchanged.

lean.statement: theorem nonempty_iso_tensorPullback_identity_relativeSplitTorus (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsLocallyNoetherian X] (hX : ∀ x : X, IsDomain (X.presheaf.stalk x) ∧ IsIntegrallyClosed (X.presheaf.stalk x)) (r : ℕ) (N : (relativeSplitTorus X r).X.left.Modules) [N.IsInvertible] : Nonempty ((tensorPullback (relativeSplitTorus X r).X.hom).obj ((tensorPullback (η[(relativeSplitTorus X r).X]).left).obj N) ≅ N)
lean.note: Uses the existing relativeSplitTorus, whose underlying scheme is canonically the stated Laurent space. Its Over structure map is q and its group identity section is e (Hopf counit z^m ↦ 1). Both inverse images use the recorded tensorPullback functor. Added the already landed definition node to stmt_deps; no new definition or statement correction.
